description: Hard: a password-reset design whose token generation, hashed storage, expiry, single use and argon2id are sound, but which leaks the token in the URL to third-party scripts and an external link, keeps existing sessions alive after reset, enables account enumeration, and lacks rate limiting; a correct answer finds the real gaps without flagging the sound parts.

security-engineer.task: Threat model the proposed password-reset design in `{fixture}/design.md` before any code is written. Report only real risks; do not pad. You cannot write files in this run, so put your complete threat model (findings with severity and remediation) in your final message.

rubricPoints.requirement: Identifies that the reset token in the `/reset` URL can leak to the third-party analytics/chat scripts and via the Referer header when the user follows the `help.example.com` link, and recommends a fix such as removing third-party scripts from `/reset`, a strict `Referrer-Policy`, and/or exchanging the token for a short-lived session before rendering the form.
Flags that existing sessions and 30-day refresh tokens survive a reset, so an attacker who already has a session keeps access, and recommends revoking all sessions and refresh tokens on reset.
Flags that the different messages for known and unknown emails on `/forgot` allow account enumeration and recommends one generic response.
Recommends rate limiting `/forgot` (per account and/or per IP), naming a harm such as email flooding of victims or bulk enumeration.
Does not claim the token generation (32 CSPRNG bytes), hashed token storage, 60-minute expiry, single-use flag, or argon2id hashing is weak or insecure.
